7e56401bd · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 06, 12:41

Draft checked bound annotations: written contracts for bounds across boundaries

no-behaviour-change

Why

Pretext (chenglou/pretext at 0d102a5c) verifies whole only after 481 checked reads (defined, present) and 57 index writes rewritten as splice, which cost measured time: in the benchmark rows slower in both runs, the splices account for most of the preparation rows' slowdown in Chrome, Firefox and webkit-host, and the checked reads for most of Firefox's layout slowdown. The bounds those reads and writes need come from callers and records: parameter ranges, result lengths, parallel arrays. A bound proved inside one function (the index-bound design of TScert #104) cannot reach them, and #104's decision P leaves open how a caller's bound crosses the call.

addedDocs docs/drafts/checked-bound-annotations.md

A design draft, for an RFC. It proposes #104's decision P, second route: the programmer writes @requires, @ensures and record @invariant clauses in JSDoc, as linear integer constraints over parameters, fields, lengths and old values. TScert checks every clause at the definition and at every call, and infers the local linear facts inside a unit. The design generalizes the callable precondition and promise of the elements fact (Effect.requires, Effect.elements) and correctness specifications' knowledge contract, with one plan constructor shared with that design. It states the clause language and its integer meaning, the elaboration to stored knowledge, the obligations at definition, call and record write, public entry points, function values, captures, the linear certificate steps, the arithmetic bridge, the trust rows, the error reports, the stated limits, the measured motivation with labelled estimates, an annotated pretext example (zeros, getHanKerningTrims) and nine owner decisions.

modifiedDocs REFERENCES.md

Entries for TScert issues #94 and #104, which the draft cites.

A section, the design by example, with an aspect table and the examples E1 to E30: each annotation form, order and linear atoms, guarded atoms, refused clause forms, predicates, old values and an append contract, record invariants with construction, the state between two appends and its observation points, callbacks, exceptional exits, opens, captures, function values, hook keys, public entry points and the public inventory, the automatic linear part, loop hints, the write rule's cases, non-null assertions, the length bound, error reports, refused declarations, invariant attachment, methods, imports, recursion, typed arrays, entry values and ghosts at a call, argument evaluation, natives and generic bounds, the write join, handlers, arithmetic limits and the stated limits. Section 9 is a walkthrough of getHanKerningTrims: the clauses, the entry knowledge, every obligation with what discharges it, the caller in measureAnalysis, the inputs each clause excludes, and the six checked reads and four splices of the rewrite that return to the original form. Each owner decision shows its options in source. The stated limits gain the separation of two arrays a record holds, which appending to both requires and no clause states.

f71756ca0 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 06, 21:58

Prove exact sums, differences and order of safe integers against the float model

no-behaviour-change

Why

Bound annotations (RFC #115) and the index-bound design (#104) read a number as a mathematical integer where it is a safe integer, and need i + 1, to - from and i < n on such numbers to mean the integer operations. The calculus computes them with Lean's Float, whose model had no lemma: the order of two doubles was proved only for naturals (IndexNumbers.doubleOrder_denotes), and no sum was proved exact, so no fact could say that i + 1 is one more than i.

addedDefinition the safe-integer fact

SafeInt(b, i) ⟺ |i| < 2⁵³ ∧ ((i ≥ 0 ∧ b = bitsOfNat |i|) ∨ (i ≤ 0 ∧ b = bitsOfNat |i| + 2⁶³))
(b the double's bits; both zeros denote 0)
safeIntOfBits(b) = the candidate magnitude b's fields give, with b's sign,
where encoding it again gives b; none otherwise

addedTheorem exact arithmetic on safe integers

SafeInt(x, i)SafeInt(y, j)|i + j| < 2⁵³⟹SafeInt(x + y, i + j)
SafeInt(x, i)SafeInt(y, j)|i − j| < 2⁵³⟹SafeInt(x − y, i − j)
SafeInt(x, i)SafeInt(y, j)⟹doubleOrder(x, y) = compare(i, j)
safeIntOfBits(b) = some i⟹SafeInt(b, i)
(+ and − are the model's IEEE operations; the proof shows that rounding
a value that is an integer below 2⁵³ yields its canonical form)

Bound every built-in store's length by 2^32 - 1, a longer literal throwing a RangeError

no-behaviour-change

Why

A bound annotation reads an array's length as a safe integer, and a read xs[i] with 0 ≤ i < xs.length as a read of an element, which needs i below 2^32 - 1, where it is an array index. The calculus built a literal's store of any length: [...a, ...a] with |a| > 2^31 made a store longer than any JavaScript array, where engines throw a RangeError, so no contract could state that a length is at most 2^32 - 1, and no length was known to be an integer (RFC #115 §4.3, length admissibility).

9670f4bbc · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 07, 03:04

Verify a counter loop's writes from linear facts the producer claims at every statement entry

verified

Why

for (let j = 0; j < xs.length; j++) xs[j] = 0 was refused: its write needs bound(xs, j) at the body's entry, an exact interface, and nothing claimed facts there. With the producer proposing linear facts at every entry, these causes were established, each where it lives: - A loop test, a tested Boolean, is evaluated twice: its value, then again from its saved operands for the dispatch's refinement (compileConditionAtom). The edge into the dispatch keeps the result and drops the re-read length and the copied counter, so the comparison's facts over them were lost before the branch (Lean). - Proposed facts named cells (bindings a closure assigns), which hold no value slot: refused by the lowering (35 cases; producer). - A drop or an edge's mapping discarded every linear fact naming a slot it does not keep, so const answer = base + 2, computed from copies of base and of the literal, lost answer = base + 2 once the copies were dropped (module-init-only, fresh-separation; Lean and the search). - A field write, and a call keeping only its receiver's own locations, kept no index fact, so a counter's facts did not survive them (for-let-capture; Lean). - A bound growing at every merge kept a loop changing until the flow solver's general widening forgot the current fields read in the loop (compiler-api-entry-path: "missing field text"; producer). - Observed: library-preserving-reflection and array-spread-host verify once the entailment search runs over the facts connected to the goal rather than all held facts (its elimination stops at 400 rows).

for (let j = 0; j < xs.length; j++) s = s + xs[j]! was refused: the read is %ElementAt%(xs, j), typed T | undefined, and nothing tied the index to the length at the read, so pretext writes each such read as a checked read (xs[j] ?? missing()). export function wrong(xs: number[], v: number): number[] {
  let at = xs.length;
  const skip = (): void => {
    at = at + 2;

  xs[at] = v;

no-behaviour-change

Why

pretext's parallel arrays need flags.length === widths.length and i + 1 < xs.length (#115). A linear fact named only slots' values, so a relation between two lengths, or a length and an expression, had no form. Following the design Astra recommended (structured terms, Linear generic in its variables), a term is a value or a length, and a length atom states its equality with the length term, so the bound rules read lengths through the same entailment. A length term means an array store's length only: a string's length needs its own admissibility bound before it can be a safe integer, and stays out.

Why

pretext's helpers need i + 1 < xs.length and xs.length === ys.length (#115). The clause language read only an index below one length; the producer had no length term; a direct test of a length (if (xs.length >= 2)) lost its facts, since a loop or branch test is evaluated again from saved operands and the edge into the dispatch drops them before the branch promotes what each answer states; and === stated no fact. Each is closed in the owner of its concern: the clause's meaning in the front end, the transfer in the producer, elimination and edge entailment in heap knowledge, the step's facts in the linear layer. The clause's facts state every intermediate a safe integer, so they imply what JavaScript computes for it.

    // Written preconditions over lengths: `pair` reads `xs[i]` and `xs[i + 1]`
// under `i + 1 < xs.length`, and `both` reads two arrays at one index under
// `xs.length === ys.length`, each with no check. Their callers establish the
// clauses by a comparison with the length and by a test of the two lengths.

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i + 1 < xs.length */
function pair(xs: number[], i: number): number {
  return xs[i]! + xs[i + 1]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < xs.length && xs.length === ys.length */
function both(xs: number[], ys: number[], i: number): number {
  return xs[i]! * ys[i]!;
}

export function firstPair(xs: number[]): number {
  if (xs.length >= 2) return pair(xs, 0);
  return 0;
}

export function firstProduct(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {

Keep the producer's length facts across calls that keep the heap

verified

Why

A loop over parallel arrays calls a helper each iteration; Lean keeps every heap fact across a call whose footprint keeps the heap (call-keep), but the producer forgot every fact naming a length at any call, so the loop head lost xs.length === ys.length and the second call could not be selected at its precondition. The producer now reads the callee's declared signatures, from the environment or the module's functions, as Lean reads the selected signature's effect.

  • written-precondition-lengths positive verified → verified dot, a loop of calls, added
    // Written preconditions over lengths: `pair` reads `xs[i]` and `xs[i + 1]`
// under `i + 1 < xs.length`, and `both` reads two arrays at one index under
// `xs.length === ys.length`, each with no check. Their callers establish the
// clauses by a comparison with the length and by a test of the two lengths.

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i + 1 < xs.length */
function pair(xs: number[], i: number): number {
  return xs[i]! + xs[i + 1]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < xs.length && xs.length === ys.length */
function both(xs: number[], ys: number[], i: number): number {
  return xs[i]! * ys[i]!;
}

export function firstPair(xs: number[]): number {
  if (xs.length >= 2) return pair(xs, 0);
  return 0;
}

export function firstProduct(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {
  if (xs.length === ys.length) {
    if (xs.length > 0) return both(xs, ys, 0);
  }
  return 0;
}

// In a loop: the test's equality is kept by each call of `both`, whose
// footprint keeps the heap, so every iteration's call establishes it.
export function dot(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {
  if (xs.length !== ys.length) throw new Error("lengths differ");
  let s = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < xs.length; j++) s = s + both(xs, ys, j);
  return s;
}

// `number` (run under Node: `undefined`).

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < xs.length && xs.length === ys.length */
function at(xs: number[], ys: number[], i: number): number {
  return ys[i]!;
}

export function first(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {
  if (xs.length !== ys.length) throw new Error("lengths differ");
  ys.pop();
  if (xs.length > 0) return at(xs, ys, 0);
  return 0;

Why

while (e < to && xs[e]! !== 0) and e === n || xs[e]! are pretext's guards. Lean's branch edge already promoted the left operand's facts; the producer stated none for a logical test, so a loop head lost its bound, and typed the right operand without the left's answer. And === stated nothing on its false answer, so e === n could not exclude n.

Effect

  • derived-index-loop positive — → verified new case
    // A loop whose index is reassigned from one derived from it: `j` starts at
// `i + 1` and only grows, so `i = j` keeps `0 <= i`. Reassigning a binding,
// or leaving its scope, eliminates it from the linear facts (Fourier–Motzkin),
// keeping what they state of the others: `1 <= j` from `j = i + 1` and
// `0 <= i`.

export function runCount(xs: number[]): number {
  const n = xs.length;
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; ) {
    const v = xs[i]!;
    let j = i + 1;
    while (j < n && xs[j]! === v) j++;
    count = count + 1;
    i = j;
  }
  return count;
}
  • invalid-derived-index-loop-negative negative — → unverified new case
    // A loop reassigning its index below where it started: `i = j - 2` admits
// `i = -1`. Under Node, `runSum([1, 2])` reads `xs[-1]`, `undefined` at
// `number`, and answers `NaN`.

export function runSum(xs: number[]): number {
  const n = xs.length;
  let count = 0;
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n && count < 3; ) {
    const v = xs[i]!;
    sum = sum + v;
    let j = i + 1;
    while (j < n && xs[j]! === v) j++;
    count = count + 1;
    i = j - 2;
  }
  return sum;
}

    // A call of a function whose loop writes only its own locals keeps the
// heap: a write of a local held in a slot changes no location, so `count`'s
// signature states the empty footprint, and the bound `i < b.length` on the
// typed array survives the call (`call-keep`).

function count(xs: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) s = s + 1;
  return s;
}

export function weighted(b: Uint8Array, xs: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < b.length; i++) {
    if (count(xs) > 0) s = s + 1;
    s = s + b[i]!;
  }
  return s;
}

// does not survive it. Under Node, `total([1, 2, 3])` reads `xs[1]` of `[1]`,

function shrink(xs: number[]): boolean {
  xs.pop();
  return true;
}

export function total(xs: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) {

    s = s + xs[i]!;
  }
  return s;
}

Effect

  • facts-across-writes positive — → verified new case, 4 functions
    // Index facts kept across a step whose writes cannot touch what they read
// (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Linear facts"): a field write's location held a member
// of the field's type, so it is no store a length reads (`cursorLoop`), no
// object a path reads and no number a path's last field holds where the type
// admits none (`labelled`, `counted`); and an element write below the length
// keeps every store's length (`filled`).

type Cursor = { i: number; label: string };
type Holder = { data: number[]; count: number };

export function cursorLoop(cur: Cursor, ys: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < ys.length; j++) {
    cur.i = j;
    s = s + ys[j]!;
  }
  return s;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(cur.i) && 0 <= cur.i && cur.i < xs.length */
export function labelled(cur: Cursor, xs: number[]): number {
  cur.label = "read";
  return xs[cur.i]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < o.data.length */
export function counted(o: Holder, i: number): number {
  o.count = i;
  return o.data[i]!;
}

export function filled(xs: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) {
    xs[i] = 1;
    s = s + xs[i]!;
  }
  return s;
}

type Holder = { data: number[]; count: number };

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < o.data.length */
export function counted(o: Holder, i: number): number {
  o.data = [];
  return o.data[i]!;
}
  • invalid-facts-across-field-write-alias negative — → unverified new case
    // A write through another parameter that may be the same object: a fact of
// `b.i` does not survive `a.i = …`, a number written where a number was. Under
// Node, `aliased(c, c, [5])` with `c = { i: 0 }` reads `xs[1]`, `undefined` at
// `number`.

type Cursor = { i: number };

/** @requires safeInteger(b.i) && 0 <= b.i && b.i < xs.length */
export function aliased(a: Cursor, b: Cursor, xs: number[]): number {
  a.i = xs.length;
  return xs[b.i]!;
}

// `undefined` at `number`, and answers `NaN`.

export function drained(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) {
    ys.pop();
    s = s + xs[i]!;

// is the number the location of the view's `[[viewLength]]` holds, and no
// heap invariant sets that location apart from a program object's number
// field, so the write keeps no fact naming the count and the read after it
// is refused. Safe under Node: the view's length never changes.

type Cursor = { at: number };

/** @requires safeInteger(n) && n <= flags.length */
export function marked(flags: Uint8Array, n: number, c: Cursor): number {
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const f = flags[i]!;
    if (f === 1) c.at = i;
    s = s + f;

Effect

  • method-calls-keep-facts positive — → verified new case
    // Method calls keep the facts their signatures' footprints keep: a
// `WeakMap`'s `get` and a `Map`'s construction state the empty footprint,
// whose calls keep every heap fact (`call-keep`), so a path's length bound a
// precondition states survives the lookup (`cached`); a `Map`'s `set` states
// `{value: any, store: keep}`, which keeps every store, so a length bound
// survives it (`mapped`) (SOURCE-CONTRACTS.md, "Weak tables").

type Prepared = { segments: string[] };
const caches = new WeakMap<Prepared, number>();

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < p.segments.length */
export function cached(p: Prepared, i: number): string {
  const hit = caches.get(p);
  if (hit === undefined) return "";
  return p.segments[i]!;
}

export function mapped(xs: number[]): number {
  const m = new Map<number, number>();
  let s = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < xs.length; i++) {
    m.set(i, i);
    s = s + xs[i]!;
  }
  return s;
}

verified

Why

WeakMap.prototype.set was declared {value: any, store: keep}, which dropped path facts (p.segments.length) at every set. Audit (ECMA-262): set requires [[WeakMapData]], tests the key with CanBeHeldWeakly (a registry read, no user code), throws a TypeError otherwise, and replaces or appends an entry; delete empties one; neither runs code nor writes a property.     // A `WeakMap`'s `set` and `delete` write only the table, host state no
// location of the model holds, and state the empty footprint, so a call of
// either keeps every heap fact (`call-keep`): a path's length bound a
// precondition states survives a cache filled on a miss (`withMap`, pretext's
// `getSegmentMetrics` caches) and a deletion (`dropped`) (SOURCE-CONTRACTS.md,
// "Weak tables").

type P = { segments: string[] };
const caches = new WeakMap<P, Map<number, number>>();

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < p.segments.length */
export function withMap(p: P, i: number): string {
  let cache = caches.get(p);
  if (cache === undefined) {
    cache = new Map<number, number>();
    caches.set(p, cache);
  }
  return p.segments[i]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < p.segments.length */
export function dropped(p: P, i: number): string {
  caches.delete(p);
  return p.segments[i]!;
}

  • record-invariant-walker positive — → verified new case (pretext's line-break walkers)
    // A record invariant as a boundary contract (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Record
// invariants"), in the shape of pretext's `line-break.ts`:
// `PreparedLineBreakData` holds per-segment data in parallel, `widths` and
// the typed array `segmentFlags`, and its walkers (`countPreparedLines`,
// `walkPreparedLinesRaw`, `stepPreparedLineGeometryFromStart`) read
// `prepared.segmentFlags[i]!` below `prepared.widths.length`. The invariant
// `segmentFlags.length === widths.length` is each walker's precondition, its
// body assumes it and each call establishes it, and a fact of the result of
// `prepare`, which its return establishes from the arrays it builds, a view
// of `widths.length` elements checked at its allocation.

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length */
export type PreparedLineBreakData = {
  widths: number[];
  segmentFlags: Uint8Array;
};

export function prepare(texts: string[]): PreparedLineBreakData {
  const widths: number[] = [];
  for (const t of texts) widths.push(t.length);
  const segmentFlags = new Uint8Array(widths.length);
  if (segmentFlags.length !== widths.length)
    throw new RangeError("a view of another length");
  for (let i = 0; i < widths.length; i++)
    segmentFlags[i] = widths[i]! === 0 ? 1 : 0;
  return { widths, segmentFlags };
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i */
function isBreak(prepared: PreparedLineBreakData, i: number): boolean {
  return i < prepared.widths.length && prepared.segmentFlags[i]! === 1;
}

export function countBreaks(prepared: PreparedLineBreakData): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.widths.length; i++) {
    if (prepared.segmentFlags[i]! === 1) n++;
  }
  return n;
}

export function layout(texts: string[]): number {
  const prepared = prepare(texts);
  return countBreaks(prepared) + (isBreak(prepared, 0) ? 1 : 0);
}

    // A constructor returning a record whose arrays differ in length: `prepare`
// states the invariant of `PreparedLineBreakData` of its result, which its
// return does not establish, `segmentFlags` one element short, and is refused
// there. A walker reading below `widths.length` then reads past the view's
// end (run under Node: `countBreaks(prepare(["a"]))` reads `undefined` at
// `number` and returns 0 for a segment whose flag `undefined === 1` is not).

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length */
export type PreparedLineBreakData = {
  widths: number[];
  segmentFlags: Uint8Array;
};

export function prepare(texts: string[]): PreparedLineBreakData {
  const widths: number[] = [];

import { open, seal, type PreparedLineBreakData, type PreparedText } from "@fixture/handle";

export function prepare(texts: string[]): PreparedText {
  const widths: number[] = [];
  for (const t of texts) widths.push(t.length);

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length && this.ends.length === this.widths.length */
export type PreparedLineBreakData = {

  segmentFlags: Uint8Array;
  ends: Int32Array;

  const widths: number[] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < widths.length; i++) {
    segmentFlags[i] = widths[i]! === 0 ? 1 : 0;

  const a = new Uint16Array(texts.length);
  const b = new Float64Array(texts.length);

  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) s = s + a[i]! + b[i]!;
  return s;

  let n = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.widths.length; i++) {

  const count = flags.length;

    if (f === 1) {

/** @requires safeInteger(end) && 0 <= end */
export function clampedSum(xs: number[], end: number): number {

  const widths: number[] = [];
  for (const t of texts) widths.push(t.length);

  } satisfies PreparedLineData as unknown as PreparedText;
}

}

  const internal = getInternalPrepared(prepared);
  let n = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < internal.widths.length; i++) {
    if (internal.segmentFlags[i]! === 1) n++;
  }
  return n;
}

export function itemCount(prepared: PreparedText): number {
  const internal = getInternalPrepared(prepared);
  return internal.items === undefined ? 0 : internal.items.texts.length;

export type Data = {
  widths: number[];
  contexts: number[] | null;

export function prepare(texts: string[], contexts: number[] | null): Data {

  return 0;

// footprints"; PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Linear facts", `receiverGrows`): a push
// keeps every fact over values, paths and element counts, and every fact
// whose lengths have coefficients at most 0, the lower bounds of lengths.

export type Prepared = {
  segmentFlags: Uint8Array;
  widths: number[];
  count: number;
};

// pretext's shape: a fresh array filled in a loop bounded by a view read
// through a field; `i < p.segmentFlags.length` survives each push, so `i++`
// is a safe integer.
export function flagsOf(p: Prepared): number {
  const out: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < p.segmentFlags.length; i++) out.push(p.segmentFlags[i]!);
  return out.length;
}

// A parameter's path facts across a push to a fresh array.
/** @requires safeInteger(p.count) && 0 <= p.count && p.count < p.widths.length */
export function widthAfterPush(p: Prepared): number {
  const out: number[] = [];
  out.push(1);
  const c = p.count;
  return p.widths[c]! + out.length;
}

// `0 <= i < other.length` across a push to an array that may be `other`
// itself: the push only grows a length.
/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < other.length */
export function readAfterPush(
  out: number[],
  other: number[],
  i: number,
): number {
  out.push(0);
  return other[i]!;
}
  • invalid-array-push-length-equality negative — → unverified new case
    // A push keeps only lower bounds of its receiver's length: after `xs.push(0)`
// the equality `xs.length === ys.length` no longer holds, and the read of
// `ys` at `xs.length - 1` is refused (run under Node: `lastOf([1], [2])`
// reads `ys[1]`, `undefined` at `number`).

/** @requires xs.length === ys.length */
export function lastOf(xs: number[], ys: number[]): number {
  xs.push(0);
  if (xs.length === 0) return 0;
  return ys[xs.length - 1]!;
}

e202848f8 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 08, 01:03

Name a binding held in a cell in linear facts, so updates inside expressions bound reads

verified

Why

if (++segmentIndex >= segmentCount) and xs[at++]! keep their binding in a cell, which no fact could name (draft guarded-clauses-and-cell-terms.md). A cell's value is a path term; the existing read, int-exact, write-link and read-bridge rules derive the updates. The unit was refused at checkAssertions: the lowered entry claim held one atom twice.

addedRule cell-term, PROGRAM-TYPING.md "Terms for bindings held in cells"

a cell-held binding is a fact root at its cell slot, its value the path
value; prefix updates give the new value, postfix the old

modifiedRule lowering: entry atoms, Lowering.Flow

modifiedRule producer

a call's precondition inside a statement updating a cell read after the
update; an expression statement updating a cell applies the update first

Effect

  • cursor-nested-update positive gap → positive unverified → verified renamed from -refused
    // pretext's `normalizePreparedLineStart` steps its index in its loop's test,
// `if (++segmentIndex >= count) return 0`: an update nested in an expression
// keeps the binding in a cell (SourceFacts.lean, "Bindings held in cells"),
// whose value the linear facts name as the path `value` of the cell
// (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Terms for bindings held in cells"), so the test's
// false answer bounds the stored value and the read `flags[segmentIndex]!`
// at the loop's next iteration is below the count;
// `cursor-invariant-loop-write` is the same loop with the update a statement.

/** @invariant safeInteger(this.segmentIndex) && 0 <= this.segmentIndex */
export type Cursor = { segmentIndex: number };

export function nextMarked(flags: Uint8Array, cursor: Cursor): number {
  const count = flags.length;
  let segmentIndex = cursor.segmentIndex;
  if (segmentIndex >= count) return 0;
  while (true) {
    const f = flags[segmentIndex]!;
    if (f === 1) {
      cursor.segmentIndex = segmentIndex;
      return f;
    }
    if (++segmentIndex >= count) return 0;
    cursor.segmentIndex = segmentIndex;
  }
}
  • cell-postfix-reads positive — → verified new case
    // Postfix updates inside an index, a binding held in a cell (PROGRAM-TYPING.md,
// "Terms for bindings held in cells"): `xs[at++]!` reads at the old value
// while the cell holds the new one, pretext's `cache[cacheAt++]!` and
// `start = ends[i++]!` shapes.

/** @requires safeInteger(at) && 0 <= at && at + 1 < xs.length */
export function twoFrom(xs: number[], at: number): number {
  const first = xs[at++]!;
  const second = xs[at++]!;
  return first + second;
}

export function sumCache(cache: number[]): number {
  let cacheAt = 0;
  let s = 0;
  while (cacheAt < cache.length) s += cache[cacheAt++]!;
  return s;
}

export function spans(ends: number[]): number {
  let i = 0;
  let width = 0;
  while (i < ends.length) {
    const start = ends[i++]!;
    width += start;
  }
  return width;
}
  • invalid-cell-prefix-read negative — → unverified new case
    // A prefix update inside an index reads at the new value: `xs[++at]!` with
// `at < xs.length` reads one past the old bound, and the read is refused (run
// under Node: `nextOf([1], 0)` reads `xs[1]`, `undefined` at `number`).

/** @requires safeInteger(at) && 0 <= at && at < xs.length */
export function nextOf(xs: number[], at: number): number {
  return xs[++at]!;
}

Effect

  • literal-equality-reads positive — → verified new case, 4 functions
    // Reads bounded by a strict comparison of a safe integer with a number
// literal: its passing answer states `i = k`, its failing one `i ≠ k`, which
// with `0 <= i` gives `1 <= i` for `k = 0`.

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i <= xs.length */
export function previousOrZero(xs: number[], i: number): number {
  return i === 0 ? 0 : xs[i - 1]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i <= xs.length */
export function previousIfNonzero(xs: number[], i: number): number {
  if (i !== 0) return xs[i - 1]!;
  return 0;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i <= xs.length */
export function firstOrPreviousPositive(xs: number[], i: number): boolean {
  return i === 0 || xs[i - 1]! > 0;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < xs.length */
export function atThree(xs: number[], i: number): number {
  if (i === 3) return xs[i - 3]!;
  return 0;
}
  • invalid-literal-equality-read-wrong-answer negative — → unverified new case
    // A read on the answer a literal comparison does not bound: `i !== 0 ||`
// runs its right operand where `i` is `0`, so `xs[i - 1]!` reads `xs[-1]`.
// Under Node, `firstOrPrevious([1, 2], 0)` reads `undefined` at `number`.

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i <= xs.length */
export function firstOrPrevious(xs: number[], i: number): boolean {
  return i !== 0 || xs[i - 1]! > 0;
}

    // Reads bounded by a quantified precondition over an array's elements
// (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Quantified clauses"): `forall i in ends: …` states of
// every index of `ends` below its length that its element is a safe integer
// at most `widths.length`, so an element read at a checked index bounds a
// read and a loop over `widths` (pretext's narrowsLine, rich-inline.ts), the
// clause's terms restated through a destructured path.

/** @requires safeInteger(k) && 0 <= k && k < ends.length
 * @requires forall i in ends: safeInteger(ends[i]) && 0 <= ends[i] && ends[i] < widths.length */
export function widthAt(widths: number[], ends: number[], k: number): number {
  return widths[ends[k]!]!;
}

/**
 * @requires safeInteger(k) && 0 <= k && k < ends.length
 * @requires forall i in ends: safeInteger(ends[i]) && 0 <= ends[i] && ends[i] <= widths.length
 */
export function sumUpTo(widths: number[], ends: number[], k: number): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < ends[k]!; i++) total += widths[i]!;
  return total;
}

export type Segments = {
  widths: number[];
  segmentFlags: Uint8Array;
  letterSpacing: number;
};

/**
 * @requires data.widths.length <= data.segmentFlags.length
 * @requires forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] <= data.widths.length
 */
export function narrowsLine(data: Segments, itemSegments: number[]): boolean {
  const { widths, segmentFlags, letterSpacing } = data;
  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < itemSegments.length; index++) {
    let width = 0;
    for (let i = itemSegments[index]!; i < itemSegments[index + 1]!; i++)
      width += widths[i]! + ((segmentFlags[i]! & 4) !== 0 ? letterSpacing : 0);
    if (width < 0) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/** @requires forall i in starts: 0 <= i && i < starts.length */
export function indicesOnly(starts: number[]): number {
  return starts.length;
}

6c03bc713 · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 08, 04:48

Frame a lazy initialization: a cell written only from null or undefined keeps every fact

verified

Why

pretext's line walkers call getEngineProfile(), which caches its profile with cachedEngineProfile ??= buildEngineProfile(). The write of the module binding's cell gave the function {value: any, store: keep}, and a call at it dropped every fact over a path or a field: in stepPreparedSimpleLineGeometry the bound cursor.segmentIndex < prepared.widths.length was gone at breakableFitAdvances[start], and a walker's prepared.segmentFlags[i]! below prepared.widths.length after the call was refused ("no derivation of its cast claim"). A closed footprint could say only that values keep or change arbitrarily, though ??= writes its cell only where it holds null or undefined, which no fact over an object, a number or a store reads.

Effect

  • lazy-cache-keeps-facts positive new → verified a cached builder's call keeps a record's invariant and a cursor's bound
    // pretext's `getEngineProfile` (measurement.ts): a module binding caching an
// object built on first use, `cachedEngineProfile ??= buildEngineProfile()`,
// read by the line walkers between a record's facts and the reads they
// bound. `??=` writes the binding's cell only where it holds `null` or
// `undefined`, and `build` keeps the heap, so `getProfile` changes no
// location holding an object, a number or a store: it is within
// `{value: init, store: keep}` (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Frame conditions"). A
// call at that footprint keeps every fact over a path's objects, numbers and
// lengths: `walk` reads `prepared.segmentFlags[i]!` below
// `prepared.widths.length` after the call, and `stepped` reads at a cursor's
// field after one. `reset` writes the cell whatever it holds: its footprint
// is `{value: any, store: keep}`, and claimed at `init` it is refused at the
// write (a control in `pipeline/test.mts`).

type Profile = { epsilon: number };

let cached: Profile | null = null;

function build(): Profile {
  return { epsilon: 0.005 };
}

export function getProfile(): Profile {
  return cached ??= build();
}

export function reset(): void {
  cached = null;
}

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length */
export type Prepared = { widths: number[]; segmentFlags: number[] };

/** @invariant safeInteger(this.segmentIndex) && 0 <= this.segmentIndex */
export type Cursor = { segmentIndex: number };

export function walk(prepared: Prepared, maxWidth: number): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.widths.length; i++) {
    const limit = maxWidth + getProfile().epsilon;
    if (prepared.widths[i]! > limit && prepared.segmentFlags[i]! !== 0) count++;
  }
  return count;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(cursor.segmentIndex) && cursor.segmentIndex < prepared.widths.length */
export function stepped(prepared: Prepared, cursor: Cursor): number {
  const epsilon = getProfile().epsilon;
  return prepared.segmentFlags[cursor.segmentIndex]! + epsilon;
}
  • invalid-lazy-cache-initializer-pops negative new → refused the initializer pops the flags before the read at the last index
    // `getProfile` caches its object with `??=`, but its initializer first pops
// the record's flags: the call changes a store, so it is no initialization
// of the cell alone, and the walker's read at the last index after the call
// is refused. Run under Node, the read gives `undefined`.

type Profile = { epsilon: number };

let cached: Profile | null = null;

/** @invariant this.segmentFlags.length === this.widths.length */
export type Prepared = { widths: number[]; segmentFlags: number[] };

function build(flags: number[]): Profile {
  flags.pop();
  return { epsilon: 0.005 };
}

export function getProfile(flags: number[]): Profile {
  return cached ??= build(flags);
}

/** @requires 0 < prepared.widths.length */
export function last(prepared: Prepared): number {
  if (getProfile(prepared.segmentFlags).epsilon < 0) return 0;
  return prepared.segmentFlags[prepared.widths.length - 1]!;
}

Soundness

init_write_within proves the write within {value: init, store: keep} from the knowledge stating the location's old contents; ofClosed_holds proves a call within {value: init, …} alters no location holding an object or a number. checkUnitJson_safe's statement is unchanged: a unit's claimed footprint is still a closed footprint its runs meet.

    // A quantified fact extended across `push` (PROGRAM-TYPING.md, "Quantified
// clauses"): a normal return of `push` keeps the receiver's elements at their
// indices and appends its actual at the old length, so `forall i in xs: B`
// over the whole receiver holds after `xs.push(a)` where `B` holds of `a` at
// index `xs.length`. pretext's builder (rich-inline.ts) pushes the current
// count of widths for each item, `itemSegments.push(widths.length)`, and its
// consumer, `narrowsLine`, reads `widths` between consecutive entries.

/** @requires forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] <= widths.length */
export function extendSegments(
  widths: number[],
  itemSegments: number[],
  items: number,
): number {
  /** @invariant forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] <= widths.length */
  while (itemSegments.length <= items) itemSegments.push(widths.length);
  let total = 0;
  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < itemSegments.length; index++) {
    for (let i = itemSegments[index]!; i < itemSegments[index + 1]!; i++)
      total += widths[i]!;
  }
  return total;
}

Frame a Map's insertion: a scalar change keeps every path's objects and every length

verified

Why

pretext's buildRangeText calls getGraphemeStart, whose cache of grapheme ends per segment is a Map held in a WeakMap; Map.set stated {value: any, store: keep}, so the call dropped every fact over a path, and the read prepared.segments[i]! after it, below prepared.segments.length, was refused ("no derivation of its cast claim"). set writes the table, which no location of the model holds, and size, a number it replaces by a number: no location holding an object or a store changes, which a closed footprint could not say.

modifiedSemantics footprint changes, FOOTPRINTS.md

modifiedDefinition Lean: the change a call's footprint allows to facts

modifiedTrust native footprints: Set and Map add, set, delete, clear; Date setTime

modifiedTyping producer

modifiedWire closed footprint

"value" may be "scalar", and Within<{ value: "scalar"; … }, T>.

Effect

  • map-insert-keeps-paths positive new → verified a read below a path's length after a call inserting into a Map (refused before)
    // pretext's `getGraphemeEnds` (line-text.ts): per handle, a `Map` from a
// segment's index to its grapheme ends, kept in a `WeakMap` and filled on
// first use. A `Map`'s `set` writes its table, which no location of the
// model holds, and its `size`, a number: within `{value: scalar, store:
// keep}`, which alters no location holding an object or a store
// (SOURCE-CONTRACTS.md, "Native footprints"). So `ends` is within it too,
// and `buildText`, pretext's `buildRangeText`, reads
// `prepared.segments[i]!` below `prepared.segments.length` after each call:
// the path's object and the store's length are kept. A fact over a number
// field is not: the `size` the call sets could be any number's location.

export type Prepared = { widths: number[]; segments: string[] };

const caches = new WeakMap<string[], Map<number, number>>();

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < segments.length */
export function ends(segments: string[], i: number): number {
  let cache = caches.get(segments);
  if (cache === undefined) {
    cache = new Map<number, number>();
    caches.set(segments, cache);
  }
  let end = cache.get(i);
  if (end === undefined) {
    end = segments[i]!.length;
    cache.set(i, end);
  }
  return end;
}

export function buildText(prepared: Prepared): string {
  let text = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.segments.length; i++) {
    const end = ends(prepared.segments, i);
    text += prepared.segments[i]!.slice(end);
  }
  return text;
}

Gap

A call keeping the heap at a parameter naming a type invariant loses 0 ≤ i of a loop counter (a fact the producer claims after it), and a loop head drops the invariant's path equalities; both predate this change.

modifiedDefinition producer: linear_facts.ml

x = r.m(…)!, r.m(…) reading no x
⇝x's facts: m's postcondition at its selected signature
a proposed fact c·t ≤ d
⇝(c/g)·t ≤ ⌊d/g⌋, g the gcd of c's coefficients

Effect

  • string-length-code-points positive positive, one function more: a do loop under a written invariant
    // Code points read below a string's length: `text.codePointAt(i)!` at
// `0 <= i < text.length` is a number by `codePointAt`'s bounded signature,
// the loop's test stating `i` below the string's length, which the read of
// `text.length` states equal to it (`string-length`). A code point past
// 0xFFFF is a surrogate pair's, so `i += c > 0xFFFF ? 2 : 1` stays within
// the length; a `@requires` over `text.length` bounds a helper's index, and
// a written `@invariant` a `do` loop's position.
// Stands for pretext's `needsComplexTextPath`, `mayHoldCursive`,
// `getScriptFactsAt` and `isEastAsianSegmentBreak`.

export function astral(text: string): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    if (text.codePointAt(i)! > 0xffff) count++;
  }
  return count;
}

export function codePoints(text: string): number {
  let count = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length;) {
    const c = text.codePointAt(i)!;
    i += c > 0xffff ? 2 : 1;
    count++;
  }
  return count;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 0 <= i && i < text.length */
function after(text: string, i: number): number {
  const c = text.codePointAt(i)!;
  const next = i + (c > 0xffff ? 2 : 1);
  return next < text.length ? text.codePointAt(next)! : -1;
}

export function second(text: string): number {
  return text.length > 0 ? after(text, 0) : -1;
}

// A read of the empty string's length, and of an astral one's.
export function lengths(): number {
  return "".length + "\u{1F600}".length;
}

function isSpace(c: number): boolean {
  return c === 0x20;
}

// A code point assigned in a `do` loop from a position bounded by a
// precondition and a test, under a written invariant over the string's
// length.
/** @requires safeInteger(end) && 0 <= end */
export function lastCodePoint(text: string, end: number): number {
  if (end >= text.length) return -1;
  let pos = end;
  let cp: number;
  /** @invariant safeInteger(pos) && 0 <= pos && pos < text.length */
  do {
    cp = text.codePointAt(pos)!;
    pos += cp > 0xffff ? 2 : 1;
  } while (isSpace(cp) && pos < text.length);
  return cp;
}

/** @requires forall i in segmentItems: safeInteger(segmentItems[i]) && 0 <= segmentItems[i] && segmentItems[i] < hyphenWidths.length */
export function hyphenRooms(hyphenWidths: number[], itemSegments: number[], segmentItems: Int32Array): number[] {
  const rooms: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < segmentItems.length; i++) {
    const index = segmentItems[i]!;
    rooms.push(i === itemSegments[index] ? 0 : hyphenWidths[index]!);
  }
  rooms.push(0);
  return rooms;
}

Prove quantified preservation through the complete element-write execution

no-behaviour-change

Why

The cell-update lemmas describe two final heaps. A bounded source write reads its store, changes an element or fills a hole, and writes the resulting store back. Preservation must cover that complete execution.

addedTheorem element-write execution

A postcondition proved for both the existing-cell update and the
fresh-cell update holds on normal return of the complete write.
Both cases include the final store update.

addedTheorem quantified clauses across the complete write

A quantified clause holds after the write when the stores and element
cells are apart, the quantified store differs from each written cell,
and the array path, bound and free terms retain their values through
either possible update. The existing-cell and hole-fill proofs establish
the two cases of the execution theorem.

Gap

The executable bounded-write checker has no element-region evidence in its heap knowledge. Allocation, renaming, reads, joins and effect filtering must establish and transport that evidence before the checker can use this theorem. The two freshness-write cases remain gaps.

Soundness

The proof uses the existing small-step semantics and safety predicate. No acceptance premise, source contract or trust assumption changes.

// clauses"): a normal return of `push` keeps the receiver's elements at their

/** @requires forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] <= widths.length */
export function extendSegments(
  widths: number[],
  itemSegments: number[],
  items: number,
): number {
  /** @invariant forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] <= widths.length */
  while (itemSegments.length <= items) itemSegments.push(widths.length);
  let total = 0;
  for (let index = 0; index + 1 < itemSegments.length; index++) {
    for (let i = itemSegments[index]!; i < itemSegments[index + 1]!; i++)
      total += widths[i]!;
  }
  return total;
}

addedDefinition heap-dependent element regions

A raw store names its element cells. An array reached through an object
path names its store cell and its element cells. Every named location
is allocated. Two regions are apart when every location of one differs
from every location of the other.

addedTheorem allocated region transfers

Literal allocation separates fresh cells from allocated old views.
Object construction adds a fresh store cell. Renaming, field reads,
heap extension and intersections of incoming evidence preserve regions.
Growth preserves separation when each added cell is fresh and the
other region's reads remain valid.

An apart-region premise supplies the store and element separation for
the complete write execution theorem. Preservation of the quantified
path, bound and free terms remains an explicit premise.

Gap

Regions are not yet fields of executable checker knowledge. The producer, evidence wire and bounded-write checker do not consume them. The two freshness write cases retain gap expectations. Fresh result store identity alone does not supply fresh element cells for native results.

Why

Pretext's pair-table read shifts a column offset by three before adding it to a row times 28. Its class lookup masks a code point by 255. Indexhood alone does not bound either result against its table.

addedRule linear facts: bounded signed shift

a and k safe integers0 ≤ a < 2³¹k checked constant0 ≤ k < 32
r = a >> k establishes integer r and 0 ≤ r, 2ᵏr ≤ a ≤ 2ᵏr + 2ᵏ − 1

addedRule linear facts: bounded mask

a and m safe integers0 ≤ a < 2³¹m checked constant0 ≤ m < 2³¹
r = a & m establishes integer r and 0 ≤ r ≤ m, r ≤ a

addedTheorem conversion and bitwise numeric results

A nonnegative safe integer below 2³¹ survives ToInt32 unchanged.
Under the rule's premises, signed right shift computes division by
2ᵏ and conjunction yields a nonnegative integer below both operands.
The arithmetic postcondition establishes the stated linear facts.

Effect

  • table-constant-stride positive gap → verified five functions including shifted and masked columns
    // Pretext's shouldBreakFast and nextBreakablePosition multiply a row by
// the fixed stride 28. The clause states the byte offset's bound.
/** @requires safeInteger(row) && 0 <= row && 28 * row + 27 < table.length */
export function lastCell(table: Uint8Array, row: number): number {
  return table[row * 28 + 27]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(row) && 0 <= row && 28 * row + 27 < table.length */
export function firstCell(table: Uint8Array, row: number): number {
  return table[28 * row]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(row) && -10 <= row && row <= 0 && 280 < table.length */
export function negativeStride(table: Uint8Array, row: number): number {
  return table[row * -28]!;
}

// Pretext's pair-table column is the code-unit offset divided by eight.
/** @requires safeInteger(row) && safeInteger(column) && 0 <= row && row <= 222 && 0 <= column && column <= 222 && 6244 <= table.length */
export function shiftedColumn(table: Uint8Array, row: number, column: number): number {
  const byte = column >> 3;
  return table[row * 28 + byte]!;
}

// Pretext's getClass selects the low byte of a Unicode code point.
/** @requires safeInteger(codePoint) && 0 <= codePoint && codePoint <= 1114111 && 256 <= table.length */
export function maskedColumn(table: Uint8Array, codePoint: number): number {
  const byte = codePoint & 255;
  return table[byte]!;
}
  • invalid-table-constant-stride negative refused → refused row-end read remains out of bounds
    // The row starts within the table; its last cell can be past the end.
// lastCell(new Uint8Array(28), 1) is undefined under Node.
/** @requires safeInteger(row) && 0 <= row && 28 * row <= table.length */
export function lastCell(table: Uint8Array, row: number): number {
  return table[row * 28 + 27]!;
}

Soundness

Conversion, quotient and conjunction facts are proved against the numeric semantics. The checker proves the range and constant premises before retaining any result facts. No trust assumption changes.

/** @requires safeInteger(k) && 0 <= k && k < items.length && safeInteger(v) && 0 <= v && v < widths.length && v <= 2147483647 && safeInteger(j)

export function writeThenRead(widths: number[], items: Int32Array, k: number, v: number, j: number): number {
  items[k] = v;
  if (j < 0 || j >= items.length) return 0;
  return widths[items[j]!]! + widths[items[k]!]!;

/** @requires safeInteger(limit) && 0 <= limit && limit < widths.length && limit <= 2147483647
 * @requires forall i in items: safeInteger(items[i]) && 0 <= items[i] && items[i] < widths.length */
export function clampAll(widths: number[], items: Int32Array, limit: number): number {
  for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
    if (items[i]! > limit) items[i] = limit;

/** @invariant this.segments.length === this.widths.length */
export type Prepared = { widths: number[]; segments: string[] };

export function ends(prepared: Prepared, i: number): number {
  return prepared.widths.length + i;
}

export function buildText(prepared: Prepared): string {
  let text = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < prepared.segments.length; i++) {
    const e = ends(prepared, i);
    text += prepared.segments[i]!.slice(e);
  }
  return text;
}

    /**
 * Arithmetic on numbers: the double operation on two operands the number
 * test answers for, yielding the number family and never a singleton. A
 * compound assignment or an increment evaluates its target's parts once,
 * reads the current value at the storage contract, and writes the result
 * back; a postfix increment is the old value.
 */
/** A sum of two numbers, and of a sum and a literal. */
function sum(a: number, b: number): number {
  const c = a + b;
  return c - 1;
}
/** A compound assignment to a mutable local. */
function plusLocal(count: number): number {
  let total = count;
  total += 1;
  return total;
}
/** A compound assignment to a field, then a read of it. */
function plusField(box: { value: number }): number {
  box.value *= 2;
  return box.value;
}
/** A postfix increment of a field is the old value. */
function increment(): number {
  const box: { value: number } = { value: 0 };
  const old = box.value++;
  return old + box.value;
}
/** The computed key's effect happens once, before the read and the write. */
function annotatedCompoundKey(): number {
  const box: { value: number } = { value: 1 };
  let count = 0;
  box[(count += 1) === 1 ? "value" : "value"] += 1;
  return count;
}
/** A postfix increment of an element access. */
function computedUpdate(): number {
  const box: { value: number } = { value: 0 };
  let count = 0;
  return box[(count += 1) === 1 ? "value" : "value"]++;
}

/** Equality merges the zeros; arithmetic must retain their sign. */
function signedZero(): boolean {
  const z = 0 * (0 - 1);
  return 1 / (1 / z + 1 / 0) === 0;
}
/** Literal type zero includes both signed runtime zeros. */
function negativeZeroLiteral(): 0 {
  return -0;
}
function zeroParameter(value: 0): number {
  return 1 / value;
}

// A labeled block left early, as pretext's line walker leaves `decided`.
export function decide(widths: number[], limit: number): number {
  let end = -1;
  decided: {
    let i = 0;
    for (const w of widths) {
      if (w > limit) {
        end = i;
        break decided;
      }

    }

  }

}

// A `continue` of the outer loop from the inner one runs the outer update.
export function rowsWithout(row: number[], banned: number[]): number {
  let kept = 0;
  let r = 0;
  outer: for (; r < banned.length; r++) {
    for (const v of row) if (banned.includes(v)) continue outer;
    kept++;
  }

export function lastKind(rows: number[][]): string | number {
  let kind: string | number = 0;
  let r = 0;
  outer: for (const row of rows) {
    r++;
    for (const v of row) {
      if (v < 0) {
        kind = "skipped";
        continue outer;
      }
    }
    kind = r;
  }
  return kind;
}

// A loop with a binding per iteration, which a closure captures, continued
// from a nested loop: each closure sees its own iteration's `i`.
export function captured(row: number[], n: number): number {
  const reads: (() => number)[] = [];
  outer: for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    for (const v of row) if (v === i) continue outer;
    reads.push(() => i);
  }
  let sum = 0;
  for (const read of reads) sum += read();
  return sum;
}

// Two labels on one loop; a `break` of a `switch` inside it, and a `break`
// of the outer label from the `switch`.
export function chained(codes: number[]): number {
  let seen = 0;
  a: b: for (const c of codes) {
    switch (c) {
      case 0:
        continue a;
      case 1:
        break;
      case 2:
        break b;
    }
    seen++;
  }
  return seen;
}

// A `finally` between the jump and its label runs on the way out, and one
// replacing the jump replaces it.
export function finals(rows: number[][]): string {
  let log = "";
  outer: for (const row of rows) {
    try {
      for (const v of row) {
        if (v === 1) continue outer;
        if (v === 2) break outer;
      }
    } finally {
      log += "f";
    }
    log += "r";
  }
  return log;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(k) && 0 <= k && k < ends.length
 * @requires forall i in ends: safeInteger(ends[i]) && 0 <= ends[i] && ends[i] < widths.length */
export function afterFreshWrite(widths: number[], ends: number[], k: number): number {

// while an unrelated, freshly allocated array grows and receives element
// writes.
/** @requires forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] < widths.length */
export function build(widths: number[], itemSegments: number[]): number {
  const scratch: number[] = [0];
  let sum = 0;
  /** @invariant forall i in itemSegments: safeInteger(itemSegments[i]) && 0 <= itemSegments[i] && itemSegments[i] < widths.length */
  for (let k = 0; k < itemSegments.length; k++) {
    scratch.push(sum);
    if (k < scratch.length) scratch[k] = -1;
    sum += widths[itemSegments[k]!]!;
  }
  return sum;
}

Why

The invariant, added to the target after census L, held after getBreakRules and was lost at the loop head. The producer forgot it on the back edge three ways: the update lastLast = last, last = text.charCodeAt(i), i++, a comma expression, was read as one statement writing the heap; the comma makes lastLast, last and i cells, and a cell's write kept only facts rooted at parameters; and keepAll && shouldKeepAfterKeepAll(rules, …) stated nothing of the call's postcondition. The checker keeps each: the cells' separation keeps them apart from the fields of every older binding's record, and both paths of the conjunction hold the invariant.

modifiedRule producer: a statement's facts

Effect

  • loop-update-keeps-field-facts positive — → verified new case
    // A loop whose update assigns bindings in a comma expression, which makes
// them cells, and whose body tests `flag && keeps(r)`: a type invariant over
// a local object's number fields holds at each call needing it. Each cell's
// write leaves the fields of the older object `r` alone, the string method
// in the update keeps the heap, and `keeps(r)`, which writes no binding
// named `r`, states the invariant again where it runs (pretext's
// `getBlinkLineBreaks`).

/** @invariant safeInteger(this.count) && 0 < this.count && safeInteger(this.width) && this.width === this.count + 3 */
export type Rules = { count: number; width: number };

export function make(): Rules {
  return { count: 1, width: 4 };
}

export function use(r: Rules): number {
  return r.width - r.count;
}

export function keeps(r: Rules, c: number): boolean {
  return c > r.count;
}

export function walk(text: string, flag: boolean): number {
  const r = make();
  let s = 0;
  let last = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < text.length; last = text.charCodeAt(i), i++) {
    if (flag && keeps(r, last)) continue;
    s = use(r);
  }
  return s;
}

export function buildRangeText(

/** @requires safeInteger(i) && 1 <= i && i < s.length && 36481 <= table.length */
export function kanaTable(s: string, i: number, table: Float64Array): number {
  const first = s.charCodeAt(i - 1);
  const second = s.charCodeAt(i);
  if (first < 0x3041 || first > 0x30ff || second < 0x3041 || second > 0x30ff) return 0;
  const index = (first - 0x3041) * 191 + second - 0x3041;
  return table[index]!;
}

/** @requires safeInteger(n) && 0 <= n && n < items.length && safeInteger(v) && 0 <= v && v < widths.length && v <= 2147483647 && safeInteger(j)

export function extendPrefix(widths: number[], items: Int32Array, n: number, v: number, j: number): number {
  const next = n + 1;
  items[n] = v;
  if (j < 0 || j >= next) return 0;
  return widths[items[j]!]!;

/** @requires widths.length <= 2147483647 */
export function buildPrefix(widths: number[]): number {
  const items = new Int32Array(widths.length);
  let n = 0;
  /** @invariant safeInteger(n) && 0 <= n && n <= items.length && n <= 2147483647 && items.length === widths.length && forall i < n of items: safeInteger(items[i]) && 0 <= items[i] && items[i] < widths.length */
  while (n < items.length) {
    const next = n + 1;
    items[n] = n;
    n = next;
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) total += widths[items[j]!]!;
  return total;
}

  while (n < size) total += items[n++]!;
  return total;

  while (n < items.length) items[n++] = 0;
  let total = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) {

export function afterAtomic(atomic: boolean[], starts: number[] | null, text: string): number {
  let total = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < atomic.length; k++) {
    if (!atomic[k]) continue;
    let after = ((starts ?? missing())[k] ?? missing()) + 1;
    while (after < text.length && text.charCodeAt(after) === 0) after++;
    total += after;
  }
  return total;
}

export function catchMissing(fail: boolean): number {
  try {
    return (fail ? missing() : 1) + 1;
  } catch {
    return 0;
  }
}

    // Each assignment propagates the literal by one binding per iteration.
type Trims = { trims: number[] | null };

export function sumTrims(record: Trims, n: number): number {
  let a = 0;
  let b = 0;
  let c = 0;
  let d = 0;
  let e = 0;
  let f = 0;
  let sum = 0;
  for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
    if (record.trims !== null) sum += record.trims[k] ?? 0;
    f = e;
    e = d;
    d = c;
    c = b;
    b = a;
    a = 1;
  }
  return sum + a + b + c + d + e + f;
}

bcd9c01ef · Cristiano Calcagno · Nov 09, 05:46

Keep a closure's program alike under its signatures where a narrowed slot is empty

verified

Why

The overloads case lost verification: guardedOverload and overloadAtNull were refused with "a closure's body lowers differently under one of its signatures". The closure (x: boolean | null) => { if (x === null) return null; return x; } advertises (x: boolean) => boolean and (x: null) => null. Under the second, return x reads x narrowed to nothing, and the lowering ended that path with a stop after the read, an empty result, while under the first it continued. The two programs differed, and one closure runs one program, so the closure was refused. invalid-overload failed with the same refusal instead of its own.

modifiedLowering operations with an empty result

Effect

  • overloads positive refused → verified each signature lowers the body to one program
    // One closure advertising two signatures. Each is a separate obligation on the
// same body, and the producer states what that body claims under each.
// TypeScript rejects the assignment: it checks the implementation's declared
// signature against each member rather than re-checking the body, so
// `(x: boolean | null) => boolean | null` is not assignable to
// `(x: boolean) => boolean`. The verifier checks the body under each signature
// and both hold, which is why this witness is the OCaml producer's alone.
function guardedOverload(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const pick: ((x: boolean) => boolean) & ((x: null) => null) = (
    x: boolean | null,
  ): boolean | null => {
    if (x === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return x;
  };
  return pick(seed);
}
function overloadAtNull(seed: boolean): null {
  const pick: ((x: boolean) => boolean) & ((x: null) => null) = (
    x: boolean | null,
  ): boolean | null => {
    if (x === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return x;
  };
  const chosen: boolean = pick(seed);
  const done: null = pick(null);
  return chosen ? done : done;
}

// Each signature retains the same captured storage contract. A row cannot
// invent a stronger current-content assertion for that captured location.
function overloadCapture(seed: boolean): boolean {
  const cell: { value: boolean } = { value: seed };
  const pick: ((x: boolean) => boolean) & ((x: null) => null) = (
    x: boolean | null,
  ): boolean | null => {
    if (x === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return cell.value;
  };
  return pick(seed);
}
  • invalid-overload negative refused → refused refused for the signature the body does not implement
    function fabricatedOverload(seed: boolean): true {
  const pick: ((x: boolean) => true) & ((x: null) => null) = (
    x: boolean | null,
  ): boolean | null => {
    if (x === null) {
      return null;
    }
    return x;
  };
  return pick(seed);
}

Soundness

The lowering only chooses the program's shape; the checker certifies the program it is given. A node whose context holds an empty slot is never reached, and so is its continuation, which the branch rules already discharge.
